item.title: Scientists found Homo erectus 200,000 years earlier than expected
item.description: New fossils from South Africa are reshaping the story of early human evolution. Researchers have described 18 hominin fossils from Drimolen Cave, including an adult Homo erectus skull fragment dated to about 2 million years ago, supporting evidence that the species appeared in southern Africa roughly 200,000 years earlier than long thought. The finds also reveal that Paranthropus robustus, which lived alongside Homo erectus, was gradually evolving even larger teeth and stronger chewing muscles as the climate changed. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: Zinave National Park in Mozambique experienced severe wildlife loss during a 16-year civil war, which impacted biodiversity. The introduction of 250 elephants has helped restore the park's ecosystem and enhance habitats for various species. Conservation programs and anti-poaching strategies have also been implemented to protect newly introduced wildlife. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: New crocodile species found fossilized in stone used to build Egypt’s Great Sphinx
item.description: A new species of extinct crocodile from Egypt has been discovered, sharing more than just its home with the Great Sphinx. Herugavialis cairensis was found in the very same rocks used to build the iconic monument. And, just as the Sphinx is famously missing the tip of its nose, the fossil crocodile is also missing the tip of its snout. Publicado también por: Phys.org. Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: 3,000-year-old horse buried inside ancient Egyptian fortress may have been a chariot animal
item.description: Archaeologists have uncovered the remains of a 3,000-year-old young male horse inside Egypt’s ancient Abqaa’ fortress, suggesting it may have been used to pull a chariot. Nearby harness fittings point to its military role. Excavations also uncovered tablets bearing the names of Ramesses II and Merneptah, along with a depiction of a captured Libyan prisoner from the Meshwesh tribe. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Bel review – a tearful, heartbreaking tribute to a spellbinding singer
item.description: Beldina Odenyo was on the verge of stardom when she took her own life in 2021. In this beautiful documentary, her grief-stricken sister Leah attempts to finish her album – and her journey will make you cry again and again In 2021, the Kenyan-Scottish singer-songwriter Beldina Odenyo was on the brink of major stardom. That October, aged 31, she headlined a gig at Edinburgh’s Usher Hall, delivering an instantly legendary performance; barefoot, cloaked and bone-shaking in its intensity. Everyone in that concert hall knew they were witnessing something extraordinary that night. Two weeks later… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.
